$comment: Our own multiplayer strings (PLAN LOC-02), merged into the en-us MP localization by scripts/balatro/build-game-pack.py. Same shape as a game localization table. English is authoritative; a translation goes in extra-strings.<lang>.json with the same keys (a key missing there falls back to English). Keys start with rmh_mp_ (except names the engine derives, such as k_trap for the Trap set, b_trap_cards, undiscovered_trap, and content descriptions such as Back.b_mp_echodeck) and must not collide with the mod's keys (the builder fails if they do). Keep the text to characters the game fonts draw: the builder checks every shipped string against the glyph bitmap.

b_mp_echodeck.name: Echo Deck
text: {C:attention}Retrigger{} all playing cards
{C:red}X1.2{} base Blind size
Increases by {C:red}X0.2{} each Ante

undiscovered_trap.name: ??? Trap Card
text: Drafted by an
opponent - reacts
to something you do

rmh_mp_to_p1t1.name: Uncommon Tag
text: {C:attention}Uncommon Tags{} take the next Joker from the game long
{C:chips}Uncommon Joker Queue{}, the same {C:chips}queue{} the shop draws its
Uncommon Jokers from. Every Joker a tag takes advances this
{C:chips}queue{}, so the Uncommon Jokers in your later shops will no
longer line up with your nemesis's. You will sometimes see
players taking Uncommon skips for extra variance, as it is
an extra chance for an {C:attention}Idol{}, {C:attention}Dusk{}, or {C:attention}Mime{} that your nemesis
will not see at the same time

rmh_mp_to_p1t2.name: Voucher Tag
text: {C:attention}Voucher tags{} advance the {C:chips}Voucher queue{}. They do this in the
same manner that seeing another ante does. For a more in
depth explanation with examples see the {C:chips}Shop Queue{} tab

rmh_mp_to_p1t3.name: Riff-raff / Top Up
text: Both {C:attention}Riff-Raff{} and {C:attention}Top Up Tag{} take the next Common Jokers
from the game long {C:chips}Common Joker Queue{}, the same {C:chips}queue{} the
shop draws its Common Jokers from. Every Joker they create
advances this {C:chips}queue{}, so the Common Jokers in your later
shops will no longer line up with your nemesis's

rmh_mp_to_p1t4.name: Orbital Tag
text: Only change is standardization between {C:attention}Mac{} and {C:attention}Windows{}. Can
still desync if players have different hands unlocked

rmh_mp_to_p1t5.name: Rare Tag / Wraith
text: {C:attention}Rare Tags{} and {C:spectral}Wraith{} take the next Joker from the game long
{C:chips}Rare Joker Queue{}, the same {C:chips}queue{} the shop draws its Rare
Jokers from. Every Joker they create advances this {C:chips}queue{}, so
the Rare Jokers in your later shops will no longer line up
with your nemesis's. A {C:attention}Rare Tag{} does nothing if you already
own every Rare Joker

rmh_mp_to_p2t1.name: Aura
text: {C:spectral}Aura{} works on a {C:chips}game long queue{}. This is how {C:spectral}Aura{} works in
Vanilla

rmh_mp_to_p2t2.name: Rare Tag / Wraith
text: {C:spectral}Wraith{} and {C:attention}Rare Tags{} take the next Joker from the game long
{C:chips}Rare Joker Queue{}, the same {C:chips}queue{} the shop draws its Rare
Jokers from. Every Joker they create advances this {C:chips}queue{}, so
the Rare Jokers in your later shops will no longer line up
with your nemesis's

rmh_mp_to_p2t3.name: Judgement
text: {C:tarot}Judgement{} takes the next Joker from the {C:chips}Joker queue{} of the
rarity it rolls, the same {C:chips}queues{} the shop uses. On
{C:attention}Black Stake+{}, where Eternal Jokers can appear in the shop,
the rarity roll comes from its own {C:chips}queue{}, so Judgement does
not change which rarities your shop rolls next. Judgement's Joker
is still drawn from the shared rarity {C:chips}queue{}, never its own: it
takes the first Joker that {C:attention}has no sticker{}, because the shop
pulls stickered Jokers from a separate {C:chips}queue{}

rmh_mp_to_p3t1.name: Glass
text: Despite {C:tarot}Justice{} being {C:red}banned{}, Glass is still avalable in
Standard Packs and via the {C:spectral}Familiar{}, {C:spectral}Grim{}, and {C:spectral}Incantation{}
Spectral cards. Glass however, has been changed to give
{C:mult}1.5x mult{} on trigger, rather than the {C:mult}Vanilla 2x{}.
Additionally, Glass breaks work on a {C:chips}game long queue{}.

rmh_mp_to_p3t2.name: Lucky
text: Lucky cards work on 2 game long {C:chips}queues{}. One for the {C:green}1/5{}
chance to hit mult. One for the {C:green}1/15{} chance for {C:money}$20{}. This is
the same way Lucky cards work in Vanilla

rmh_mp_to_p3t3.name: Purple Seal
text: {C:attention}Purple Seals{} take from the {C:chips}Up Top Tarot Queue{}

rmh_mp_to_p4t1.name: Orange Deck
text: Multiplayer Exclusive. Start run with a {C:attention}Giga Standard Pack{}
(Read more about this in the Packs tab). Start run with 2
copies of Hanged Man

rmh_mp_to_p4t2.name: Violet Deck
text: Multiplayer Exclusive. 1 additional Voucher Slot. During
{C:attention}Ante 1{}, Vouchers are {C:money}50% off{}, and during {C:attention}Ante 2{}, they are
{C:money}30% off{}

rmh_mp_to_p5t1.name: Superposition +
text: These 3 Vanilla Jokers work as expected, with the Tarot
cards they give taken from the {C:chips}Up Top Tarot Queue{}

rmh_mp_to_p5t2.name: Prob. Jokers
text: The 6 Vanilla Jokers shown below work basically as expected,
each operating on its own {C:chips}game long queue{} that progresses
every time you trigger the Joker. {C:attention}8-Ball{} and {C:attention}Hallucination{}
take from the {C:chips}Up Top Tarot Queue{}. {C:attention}Oops All 6s{} doubles the
number that must be rolled less than

rmh_mp_to_p5t3.name: Golden Ticket
text: {C:attention}Golden ticket{} has been changed in a couple ways. It is now
{C:attention}Uncommon Rarity{} instead of Common, and it no longer requires
the player to have a gold card in the deck to appear in
shop. It still gives {C:money}$4{} for each Gold card scored

rmh_mp_to_p5t4.name: Seance / Sixth Sense
text: {C:attention}Seance{} and {C:attention}Sixth Sense{} take the Spectral cards they generate
from the {C:chips}Up Top Spectral Queue{}. Ancient Joker, Sock and
Buskin, and Photograph work as expected

rmh_mp_to_p5t5.name: Riff-Raff / Top Up
text: Both {C:attention}Riff-Raff{} and {C:attention}Top Up Tag{} take the next Common Jokers
from the game long {C:chips}Common Joker Queue{}, the same {C:chips}queue{} the
shop draws its Common Jokers from. Every Joker they create
advances this {C:chips}queue{}, so the Common Jokers in your later
shops will no longer line up with your nemesis's

rmh_mp_to_p5t6.name: To Do List
text: {C:attention}To Do List{} is technically not changed from vanilla, besides
making sure {C:attention}Mac{} and {C:attention}Windows{} users have the same {C:attention}To Do List{}
{C:chips}queue{}

rmh_mp_to_p5t7.name: Invisible Joker
text: {C:attention}Invisible Joker{} has been changed to decrease the variance
between players on what it hits. Previously both players
could copy different joker positions independently. Now each
Joker is ranked by its own key instead of its position, so
players with the same Jokers copy the same one. If player 2
has one extra Joker on top of the N both players share, it
is hit at only {C:green}1/(N+1){} chance, with all others copying what
both players share

rmh_mp_to_p5t8.name: Bloodstone
text: {C:attention}Bloodstone{} operates on 2 seperate {C:chips}queues{}. The first is game
long and progresses every time you play a heart while {C:red}NOT{} in
a Pvp blind. {C:attention}Bloodstone{} has a {C:chips}Pvp queue{} that changes each
ante. While in Pvp, after playing a hand, {C:attention}Bloodstone{} returns
to the beginning of the {C:chips}Pvp queue{}

rmh_mp_to_p5t9.name: Idol / Mail-In Rebate
text: The {C:attention}Idol{} and {C:attention}Mail-In Rebate{} pick their card from your deck.
To keep things fair between players, the cards they choose
from are sorted by how many copies of each card your deck has,
rather than by deck order, so neither player gets an
edge from how their deck happens to be arranged

rmh_mp_to_p6t1.name: Hand Smoothing
text: Not a really important change since this type of effect is
so hard to measure. This changes the Ante based draws in
Vanilla to be Round based instead. This essentially makes
draws slightly more similar.

rmh_mp_to_p7t1.name: Arcana / Spectral
text: All Arcana, Celestial, and Spectral packs take from their
respective consumable's {C:chips}Pack queue{}. See the {C:chips}Shop Queue{} tab
for a more in depth explanation with examples

rmh_mp_to_p7t2.name: Buffoon Pack
text: Buffoon Packs take directly from the {C:chips}Shop Queue{}. Normal
Packs take the next 2 Jokers. Jumbo and Mega take the next 4
Jokers

rmh_mp_to_p7t3.name: Standard Pack
text: Standard Packs take from a game long Playing Card {C:chips}queue{}.
This {C:chips}queue{} is seperate from the {C:attention}Magic Trick{} Playing Card
{C:chips}queue{}. This does mean that if you open a Normal than a
Jumbo, it is possible you end up with 2 cards you want in
the Jumbo and none in the Normal, whereas you would have
been able to take both if you opened them in the other
order. The {C:attention}Giga Standard Pack{} from the Orange Deck shows 10
cards, lets you choose 4, cannot be skipped, and takes from
this same {C:chips}queue{}

rmh_mp_to_p8t1.name: Overview
text: The {C:chips}shop queue{} in Balatro Multiplayer differs from Vanilla
in many ways. There are 3 sections of the Shop, each with
their own {C:chips}queues{}: the Main shop, the Pack shop, and the
Voucher shop. Skipping does {C:red}NOT{} advance the {C:chips}queue{} for your
nemesis

rmh_mp_to_p8t2.name: Sub-Queues
text: The {C:chips}Main Shop Queue{} is seperated into 7 sub {C:chips}queues{}. Common
Joker Queue. {C:chips}Uncommon Joker Queue{}. {C:chips}Rare Joker Queue{}. Up Top
Tarot Queue. {C:chips}Up Top Planet Queue{}. {C:chips}Up Top Spectral Queue{}.
{C:chips}Playing Card Queue{}. Every time you see a new Shop or Reroll,
you progress the {C:chips}Main Shop Queue{}. Tags and cards that create
Jokers (Uncommon, Rare, Top Up, Riff-Raff, Wraith,
Judgement) take from the same Joker {C:chips}queues{} as the shop

rmh_mp_to_p8t3.name: How It Works
text: If {C:attention}Player 1{} skips and {C:attention}Player 2{} does not, {C:attention}Player 1{} will still
see the packs that {C:attention}Player 2{} does, just a blind after.
Rerolling only advances the {C:chips}queue{} for that player

rmh_mp_to_p9t1.name: Vouchers
text: No vouchers are changed from Vanilla itself. However, read
more about the changes to the {C:chips}Voucher queue{} (when vouchers
come up in shop) in the {C:chips}Shop Queue{} tab
